title: Handlebar Phone Dock
tagline: Turn an old phone into a permanent motorcycle navigation screen.
summary: A slim sealed phone case that slides onto a handlebar dock, locks with a key and charges through spring contacts. No cable to plug in. It fits any motorcycle with a round handlebar (22.2, 25.4 or 28.6 mm) and any phone: set your measurements and export your own parts.
status: a dimensioned concept model, version 0.5. It has not yet been tested on the road, for water, heat or vibration. Check the fit on your own bike and phone before relying on it, and use a safety tether at first.
see_sub: The video is rendered straight from the CAD: assembly, docking, the contacts, the wiring, the key lock and the over-heat cut-off.

case_shell.name: Case shell
case_shell.what: Front of the slim case: the window lip, side walls and plug bay

case_back.name: Case back
case_back.what: Back cover: O-ring tongue, cable channel, thermostat pocket

window_template.name: Window template
window_template.what: Guide for cutting the 2 mm polycarbonate window

shoe.name: Shoe
shoe.what: Plate on the case's back: dovetail rails, contact nose, lock strike

receiver.name: Dock
receiver.what: Rail channels, pogo-pin pocket, dock-board pocket, printed snap, lock pod
receiver.material: ASA or PETG, printed back face down

base_plate.name: Base plate
base_plate.what: Joins the clamps to the dock through rubber grommets
base_plate.material: ASA or PETG (or cut from base_plate.dxf)

dock_base.name: Dock base (one-piece option)
dock_base.what: The dock and base plate as one part, instead of receiver + base_plate (set mount = "merged"). Clamp spacing 132–154 mm
dock_base.material: ASA or PETG, on the lock pod's bottom face with supports under the plate

iso_pad.name: Rubber pad (one-piece option)
iso_pad.what: Sits between each clamp pad and the dock base; cut from 2 mm neoprene using it as a template, or print it

clamp_body.name: Clamp body
clamp_body.material: PETG, ASA or PA12, 100 % infill round the ring

clamp_cap.name: Clamp cap
clamp_cap.material: PETG, ASA or PA12, 100 % infill round the ring

bar_shim.name: Bar shim
bar_shim.what: Adapts the clamps to a smaller bar (or use strips of old inner tube)

pad_spacer.name: Pad spacer
pad_spacer.what: Raises the mount if the instrument cluster needs room

lock_yoke.name: Lock yoke
lock_yoke.what: Carries the steel bolt; driven by the lock's cam

lock_cover.name: Lock cover
lock_cover.what: Closes the lock pod, with a drain slot

crank_template.name: Crank template
crank_template.what: Drilling guide for the crank-pin hole in the lock's cam

strike_keeper.name: Steel keeper
strike_keeper.what: Optional steel strike; cut it from strike_keeper_2d.dxf (set steel_keeper = true)

plock_body.name: Printed lock: body
plock_body.what: Optional printed lock (instead of the store cam lock): D-shaped body with the wafer channels
plock_body.material: PETG or ASA, 100 % infill, 0.15 mm layers, flange down

plock_plug.name: Printed lock: plug
plock_plug.what: Turns with the key and drives the crank; holds the 4 wafers and 8 springs
plock_plug.material: PETG, 0.15 mm layers, lying on its flat

plock_wafer_1.name: Printed lock: wafer 1
plock_wafer_1.what: Front wafer. The 4 wafers differ (they set the key code): print your own from lock_code

plock_wafers.name: Printed lock: all 4 wafers
plock_wafers.what: The 4 wafers on one plate, in order

plock_key.name: Printed lock: key
plock_key.what: Flat key cut to lock_code (the example code here: make your own)

plock_clip.name: Printed lock: clip
plock_clip.what: C-clip that holds the body in the pod (snaps into its groove)

plock_crank.name: Printed lock: crank
plock_crank.what: Replaces the drilled steel cam: M3 insert for the crank pin, grub screw onto the plug

dxf.base_plate: The base plate as a flat outline, for cutting from sheet instead of printing
dxf.strike_keeper_2d: Optional 6 mm steel strike, for laser cutting (set steel_keeper = true)

download_note: The STLs are made for the default (placeholder) phone, 75 × 160 × 9 mm, and a 22.2 mm handlebar. For your own phone and bike, change the measurements in the source and export your own parts: see Adjust it to your hardware. The parts that depend on the phone are case_shell, case_back and window_template; the clamps and shims depend on the bar.
